newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hashimoto says Mideast not part of U.S.-Japan pact.
newsitem.headline: Hashimoto says Mideast not part of U.S.-Japan pact.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Tuesday that proposed new security arrangements with the United States do not mean Japan will be drawn into any future military conflict in the Middle East.
"If the Middle East were an 'area surrounding Japan' then anywhere else on earth will be an 'area surrounding Japan'," Hashimoto told reporters on Tuesday.

Hashimoto was referring to a new framework for U.S.-Japan military cooperation announced at the weekend following talks in Hawaii that calls on Japan to send warships to support U.S. military action in an armed conflict "surrounding Japan".

The new framework came in an interim report on a year-long review of the "Guidelines of Defence Cooperation". The report says Japan will send navy vessels on minesweeping and naval blockade operations. A final report is due in November.
The interim report does not define the geographical area covered by the new arrangements.
"It is very difficult to draw a line," one Foreign Ministry official said.
Up until now, Japan had refused to take part in any armed conflict unless attacked, saying its pacifist constitution bars it from settling international disputes by military means.
Analysts said the new framework seems to go beyond the rigid no-war tenet Japan adopted after World War Two.

Hashimoto said he instructed Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda and Defence Minister Fumio Kyuma to clarify the geographic extent of the new bilateral military agreement in order to prevent a misunderstanding with the United States.
"The measures Japan will adopt in a problem in the Middle East will come under a different category (other than the guidelines)," Hashimoto said.
